steps.prompt: Two chords cross inside a circle, cutting each other into pieces. Measure the pieces in a drawing. Do you notice anything about the products?

cards.title: One rule, three pictures
cards.body: Draw any line through a point $P$ that meets a circle at $A$ and $B$. The product $PA \cdot PB$ is the same for every such line. Chords crossing inside: $PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD$. Two lines from outside: $PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD$, with the distances measured from $P$. A tangent $PT$ counts as a line touching twice: $PT^2 = PA \cdot PB$.

cards.title: Worked example: crossing chords
cards.problem: Chords $AB$ and $CD$ cross at $P$, with $PA = 4$, $PB = 6$ and $PC = 3$. How long is $PD$?

cards.title: Using it from outside
cards.body: From an outside point, use the whole distance to the far point, not the piece inside the circle. A point inside, at distance $d$ from the centre of a circle of radius $r$, has $PA \cdot PB = r^2 - d^2$ for every chord through it (look at the diameter).

cards.title: Worked example: a tangent
cards.problem: From $P$, a line meets a circle at $A$ and then $B$, with $PA = 4$ and $PB = 9$. How long is the tangent $PT$?

cards.title: The common trap: the inside piece
cards.body: From outside, $PB$ is the whole distance from $P$ to the far point, not the chord $AB$ inside the circle. Read which length the question wants: $PB$ or $AB$.

prompts: How do you remember which lengths to multiply?
